description: Codex triage routes bounded bug fixes directly and preserves the complete design path for risky work; verification and protected review remain mandatory on every shipping route.

rules.reason: The run has returned to triage again after its one permitted reclassification; stop before another implementation, regardless of the proposed class.

A proved bounded bug fix enters implementation directly, then all shell gates and one independent security-capable reviewer.
A broader fix within existing contracts enters implementation directly, then all shell gates and independent correctness/security review.
Architecture or contract design needs the inherited contrarian positions, chief and deterministic design check before implementation.
Security, concurrency, persistence, delivery gates and accepted-contract work keep the complete inherited design and four-reviewer path.
Uncertain classification or an operator decision is a hard stop, never an implicit cheap route.
The task still exceeds its ruled scope after one return to triage; stop for the operator.
The implementer discovered broader scope and returns it once for evidence-based reclassification.

A single-review clean result with missing or inconsistent scope/fixes facts is unknown, never permission to ship.
The broader or complete review found the verified change clean without fixes; its inherited admission is unchanged.
Only explicitly safe, scoped, unchanged small-bug residuals of at most medium severity can use tracked debt.
Broader and complete review preserve the inherited explicit non-security, at-most-medium admission; unsafe or unknown residual facts still reach the inherited hard stop.
Clean but fixes applied; re-verify before shipping.
Missing, malformed or inconsistent scope/fixes facts are unknown, never permission to ship or enter a verify loop.
